options.label: supersede with ADR-004
options.consequence: moves every Governed by link of eighteen nodes and contracts for text that replaces no item as a whole

decisions.chosen: amend in place with a dated history bullet
decisions.why: No item is replaced as a whole: each change states a reading the shipped tool already takes, restates a reason, or says plainly what a set does not check. The brief and the tree's practice both call for an in-place amendment.

options.consequence: the premise still reads as if the first producing phase lands every declaration itself, which topology-ir@v1's split contradicts

options.consequence: item 10 loses the reason surface and reject run in full from the first producing phase

decisions.question: S118: 'a conformance library that no binding in any slug imports covers nothing' was routed as a reading of item 3. The shipped structure set counts every conformance library's case names toward coverage and reads one slug at a time. What does the ADR state?

options.label: the tool's reading, and every library bound as a rule checked by reading
options.consequence: item 4 requires every conformance library to be imported by a binding of its own contract or another; item 9 says structure counts an unbound library's cases and does not check binding; nothing shipped becomes wrong; a cross-slug check stays the owner's choice

options.label: covers nothing, as routed
options.consequence: makes the shipped structure set wrong (it would need every slug's bindings to judge one slug), a tool change the sweep's rule forbids

options.label: the tool's reading only
options.consequence: an unbound suite stays legitimate, so a suite that runs at no gate could cover an id with no rule against it

decisions.chosen: the tool's reading, and every library bound as a rule checked by reading
decisions.why: Stating 'covers nothing' would make a shipped behavior wrong, so the sweep's rule rules it out. A suite no binding imports runs at no gate, so requiring every library to be bound is the sound rule, and it is compatible: every committed conformance library is bound (L1, nine of nine). Whether structure should check it across slugs is a tool change, left to the owner. A careful engineer would have asked, because the routed reading is turned down.

decisions.question: S119: structure does not check that a binding imports exactly one conformance library by relative path; behavior fails it (rule suite), but --all --set structure passes it. What does the ADR say?

options.label: state the rule in item 4 and say structure leaves it to behavior
options.consequence: item 4: a binding imports exactly one conformance library, by relative path; item 9 and Consequences say plainly that only behavior checks it, so --set structure passes such a binding

options.label: have structure check it
options.consequence: a tool change, outside the sweep; left to the owner

decisions.chosen: state the rule in item 4 and say structure leaves it to behavior
decisions.why: The shipped behavior set already enforces exactly one suite (behavior.dart _planImports; probe B: none_test.dart and two_test.dart fail suite, while A passes both under --set structure). The rule is the tool's choice; the gap is only that structure does not check it, which the text now says plainly.

decisions.question: S119: the directive reader reads only the first URI of an import or export, so a conditional-configuration URI escapes src-import, conformance-import and PENDING. What does the ADR state?

options.label: ban configurations on fixture directives, said plainly unchecked
options.consequence: item 2 adds the ban with its reason; item 9 says what a configured URI escapes; no committed fixture uses one, so nothing breaks

options.label: allow them and say the tool does not read them
options.consequence: a fixture could import package:test or a src/ library, or an absent package, in a configuration, and the text would permit it

options.label: make the reader read every URI
options.consequence: a tool change (dart_library.dart _directives), outside the sweep; left to the owner

decisions.chosen: ban configurations on fixture directives, said plainly unchecked
decisions.why: A fixture never needs a configuration: conformance libraries are platform-neutral and a binding's imports pick its runner. The ban makes the reader's limit harmless. Probe A shows structure passing configured imports of package:test, a src/ library and an absent package; B shows the configured absent package failing to load instead of PENDING; L2 shows none of the 84 committed Dart fixtures uses a configuration.

options.consequence: the description names contract-text, the case names, the Validation forms with unknown ids, the Case table against the case directories, layout, src-import, conformance-import and encoding, so a reader does not mistake an unnamed rule for one that is not checked

options.consequence: smaller touch; the Case-table check and the contract-text checks stay unnamed

decisions.question: S121: item 9 says dart pub get --enforce-lockfile runs 'so that no case runs on a stale resolution', which it does not do on Dart 3.13.5. What reason does the bullet give?

options.label: what it does, and that no case needs freshness
options.consequence: it runs before the package configuration is read, so PENDING and the {package}:{executable} roots are the committed lockfile's, and a lockfile that no longer satisfies the pubspecs is an environment error of file and cli; it does not make a stale workspace fresh, and no case needs it to, since file replays run from the root and recorded invocations use the script form

options.label: drop the pub get
options.consequence: a tool change, and it loses the lockfile check before command runs

options.label: keep the stated reason
options.consequence: the ADR keeps a reason the evidence refutes

decisions.chosen: what it does, and that no case needs freshness
decisions.why: file-cli-sets-plan K, M, N and probe E show pub get leaving a stale workspace stale (here it rewrote pubspec.lock but not the package configuration, so lock is newer than config) and dart run from files/ exiting 255, while the script form runs. shell.dart runs pub get before reading the configuration (design decision 15), and a failing pub get makes every file and cli set unavailable (exit 2).

decisions.question: S121: item 7 names the {package}:{executable} command but not how it runs. What does it state, and does it say anything of a dart run command in a case with files/?

options.label: state the script form and require {package}:{executable} for a case with files/
options.consequence: item 7 says dart and flutter are the running SDK's, and a {package}:{executable} command runs as bin/{executable}.dart under the running dart with --packages, never through dart run, with the reason; a dart command whose first argument is run runs as written, so a case with files/ names an executable as {package}:{executable}, which no set checks

options.label: state the script form only
options.consequence: a later case could record dart run from files/ and read exit 255 as its own exit code on a stale workspace

options.label: have the tool run dart run in the script form too
options.consequence: a tool change, outside the sweep

decisions.chosen: state the script form and require {package}:{executable} for a case with files/
decisions.why: processOf in command.dart is the shipped form, and probe C passes a case whose recorded stdout pins it: script {root}/packages/probe_tool/bin/facts.dart, packages file://{root}/.dart_tool/package_config.json, cwd {files}, also on a stale workspace (E), where dart run exits 255. The authoring rule is compatible: no committed recorded invocation runs dart run (L6).

decisions.question: S121 and S122: behavior reports PENDING before the restriction; file and cli apply the restriction before PENDING. S122's final review asked an item 9 touch to state restriction-first. Which order does item 9 state?

options.label: each set's shipped order, defects first in all
options.consequence: item 9 states that a defect fails whatever the restriction, then file and cli restriction-first and behavior PENDING-first; nothing shipped becomes wrong; one order stays the owner's choice

options.label: restriction-first for every set
options.consequence: makes the shipped behavior set wrong (behavior.dart _planRun); a tool change

options.label: PENDING-first for every set
options.consequence: makes file and cli wrong and fails nidana.tooling.lint.1 to .4 and codegen.9 and .11, whose restricted gates rely on the other producer's absent package passing unrun

decisions.chosen: each set's shipped order, defects first in all
decisions.why: One order for all sets would make a shipped behavior wrong, which the sweep's rule forbids. The file and cli order, which the tooling gates need, is stated as S122 asked. The behavior order is compatible with every committed binding (DEC-1306 checked that each binding's packages exist by the first gate that runs it). Probes B and C show both orders and the defect-first rule. A careful engineer would have asked whether to align behavior, which is a code change.

experiments.question: For each reading the amendment states, what does the shipped replay tool do, in a copy of the committed tree with probe slugs (probe-cli, probe-file, probe-api) and a stand-in member probe_tool; and do the committed fixtures already meet the rules the amendment adds?
experiments.finding: A: --set structure passes a binding that imports no conformance library and one that imports two, an unbound conformance library whose case alone covers G2, a case named in two Case rows whose second row alone covers G5, and configured imports of package:test, a src/ library and an absent package. B: behavior fails the two bindings (suite), runs the configured binding to a load failure instead of PENDING, and reports PENDING for a binding of an absent package even under a restriction that admits none of its cases. C: cli runs a case whose plugins: line carries a comment and reports PENDING for the plain one; reads the duplicated case's ids from its first row (G5 not admitted, G4 runs); fails an unreadable exit_code under every restriction; passes unrun a case of an absent package that the restriction does not admit; runs a {package}:{executable} case as bin/{executable}.dart under --packages from files/ (its recorded stdout pins script, packages and cwd) and leaves the file it wrote in files/. D: the generator command comes from the one span with {output} and a space; a file replay with no covers clause runs unrestricted and is not run under --guarantee G1. E: with a member pubspec.yaml newer than pubspec.lock, the replay's pub get --enforce-lockfile rewrote pubspec.lock but not the package configuration, the workspace stayed stale, dart run probe_tool:facts from files/ exited 255, and the script form ran. F: dart analyze . from analyze-clean's files/, its plugins section removed, added and removed no entry below files/. L (committed tree): 9 of 9 conformance libraries bound; 0 of 84 Dart fixtures with a configured directive; no Case table names a case twice; all 8 plugins: lines exact; every file replay and recorded invocation declares ids; no recorded invocation runs dart run.
